record.title: China issues an eight-ministry framework to expand AI products, services and consumption scenarios
record.summary: China’s Ministry of Commerce and seven other departments issued an implementation opinion for “AI + consumption.” Its 17 measures cover consumer AI products and robots, home and elder-care services, tourism, hospitality and education, retail, e-commerce, logistics, demonstration clusters, an application-scene guide/open list, fiscal and consumer-credit support, infrastructure, standards and safety. The MOFCOM page marks the opinion currently effective. This is evidence of official policy intent and specified measures; it does not establish appropriations, deployment, consumer uptake, subsidy redemption or economic effects.
organizations: Ministry of Commerce of the People’s Republic of China
Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Eight Chinese government departments issued 商建发〔2026〕89号, an implementation opinion dated 2026-06-09 that the MOFCOM page marks currently effective.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The opinion sets out 17 measures spanning AI products and services, commerce and logistics, application pilots, fiscal/credit support, infrastructure, standards and safety.

evidence_gaps.description: No national appropriation, implementation progress series, provincial program-level outlays/redemptions or eligible-category sales series is established.

brief.importance_rationale: If carried into implementation, an eight-ministry framework spanning consumer AI products and services, commerce, logistics, pilots, fiscal/credit support, infrastructure and standards could shape China’s consumer-facing AI supply and deployment choices. The score reflects the stated policy scope, not evidence of spending, uptake or effects.
limitations: The opinion establishes policy intent and assigned measures, not their completion or enforcement.
No national appropriation, program-level disbursement, consumer uptake, subsidy redemption, sales baseline, deployment total or measured economic/productivity effect was found in this source review.
Earlier Hubei follow-up is one-province activity and bundles public subsidies with private promotions; it does not establish national implementation or causal impact.
organizations: Ministry of Commerce of the People’s Republic of China

technical.claimed_result: No technical performance result is claimed.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official opinion and its 17 stated measures were directly inspected in the original Chinese source.
technical.mechanism: Eight departments coordinate proposed measures across products, services, commerce, logistics, pilots, support instruments, infrastructure, standards and safety.
technical.regime: National Chinese policy framework issued 2026-06-09; one-province Hubei implementation follow-up is not treated as national uptake.
technical.strongest_baseline: The MOFCOM document itself is the primary evidence for policy issuance and stated measures; it contains no outcome baseline.

brief.title: China issues an eight-ministry framework to expand AI products, services and consumption scenarios
brief.why_it_matters: The framework connects consumer-facing AI supply and services to commerce, logistics, pilots, fiscal and credit tools, infrastructure and standards across multiple ministries. If implemented, it could influence product availability and deployment incentives. The document reports no spending, adoption or measured productivity/demand effects.
